swept: hn show hn, 3 years, 20 grudge phrases, 8 parallel verifiers
dropped: Rescript: NEAR MISS, fails gate 3 by the letter. Grudge is perfect ("Descript costs $24/mo, so I built this over a single weekend with Fable!", solo wassgha, no account, no pricing page) but the repo relicensed from MIT to PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and getrescript.com FAQ says free "for noncommercial use" with commercial licensing and "potential future server-based paid features". That is the "free for personal use" string criteria.md forbids. Override candidate if you relax that clause; Descript Hobbyist is $24/mo billed monthly per descript.com/pricing.

EmbedPDF: open-core. Grudge only "Acrobat is heavy, closed, and pricey"; repo now ships cloudpdf/server under Fair Core License requiring a paid CloudPDF license key, and embedpdf.com has an /enterprise page. Also primarily an SDK.
Hopp: open-core. "Managed cloud, 14 days free trial" at gethopp.app, sign-up required; grudge names no single victim ("high cost of existing pair programming tools").
Wakana: needs an account before you can try it (hosted, login via GitHub/email OTP); grudge and victim were fine (WakaTime Premium $14/mo).

open-source-slack-ai: victim no longer priced. Slack AI is not sold as an add-on anymore (bundled into paid plans per slack.com/pricing), and it is a self-hosted Slack bot needing deployment plus an OpenAI key.
idiotproofseo: has its own pricing page (Hobbyist $9/mo, Starter $19/mo, Pro $49/mo) and a credit-limited free tier; no named victim.
Puzzle Lair: paywall after 25 puzzles per type (one-time unlock) and account required to keep playing; victim is 'ad-supported puzzle apps', not a named paid tool.
Zipshot: team ("we", "one of the builders"), no named victim, and "free for individual users forever" is a strings-attached promise with cloud storage that expires after 3 months.
screenrecorder.me: no grudge sentence anywhere in the thread; builder repeatedly says he intends to charge ("I do want to charge", offers free service to beta testers once billing starts).
Files.md: no price grudge; builder explicitly says "I don't position it as Obsidian alternative"; Obsidian is free for personal use anyway.
Opal Editor: no grudge in story or comments; Obsidian is free for personal use.
Modo: empty story, author comments are "for fun :)"; no grudge, no single victim (Kiro/Cursor/Windsurf).
Imagin Raw: no grudge in thread; Adobe Bridge is free.
RewritePal: no grudge; only "completely free to use and requires no sign-up" with no Grammarly price complaint.
Sink: no grudge; author comments are about data ownership and QR codes, Bitly never mentioned as pain.
Arthas.AI: empty story, zero author comments; nothing to quote.
remove-your-data: not an app (an agent skill/prompt repo you paste into Claude Code etc.); victim unnamed ("a paid service").
screen.now (Screen Studio alt): no grudge sentence in the builder's own words anywhere on HN; closed source, site is a bare tool. Fails gate 1.
IF (Typora alt): freemium at $3/mo with an 'Infinity plan' and activation codes; builder is a former co-founder pitching a company product. Fails gate 3 (open-core).

Let's Split (Splitwise alt): no grudge sentence on HN or letsplit.com ('Add Unlimited Expenses' is feature copy, not a grudge); Splitwise Pro price not shown on splitwise.com/pro. Fails gates 1 and 2.
Pluely (Cluely alt): now closed source with a Pricing page, 'Get License' and a Pro license tier on pluely.com. Fails gate 3 (open-core with own paid tier).
Pebble (Minecraft Java alt): no grudge, no price complaint; a Swift rewrite for its own sake. Fails gate 1.
Zoonk (Duolingo alt): no grudge in the post; framed as 'the go-to place for learning and career development', i.e. a startup. Fails gate 1.

Chalkboard (Raspberry Pi wall display): excellent grudge ('I got tired of subscription-based wall displays and locked ecosystems, so I built my own.') but names no specific paid victim on HN, in the README, or in the repo metadata; main source repo is private. Fails gate 2.
Touch Grass IDE (Chad IDE alt): grudge is about real-money gambling in an IDE, not price; no paid victim price. Fails gate 1/2.
Voquill (Wispr Flow alt): now 'Voquill, Inc.', 'Backed by Y Combinator', pivoted to pathology dictation with 'Book a call'. Automatic reject (YC-backed).
Caley.io (Superhuman alt): marketing copy only ('your unfair advantage'), no grudge, no price. Fails gate 1.
Kanba: no grudge sentence in the post or comments, and no URL was ever posted (link promised in comments never appeared).
Cryptick: builder's grudge is Minute Cryptic's account wall, not price, and minutecryptic.com has no paid plan, so no victim price to verify.
Simpluna: not free with no strings — the builder sells optional features as one-time in-app purchases, and it is run as a Tokyo company.
JermCAD: grudge is that Fusion/OnShape were hard to learn, not their price; no paid victim named in the builder's words.
Seaquel: seaquel.app has a pricing page with commercial plans ($0-$229/year) — open-core from the same maker; no named paid victim or grudge either.
Agent Arnold: no named paid victim, and it requires Telegram OAuth or a magic-link email login before you can try it.
ScreenKite: screenkite.com sells a Pro license ($79.99 founder price, returning to $99.99) with watermarked free exports; builder's grudge is export speed, not Screen Studio's price.
FreeGuessr: 'We built' team, site is JS-only with no about text, and no grudge about GeoGuessr's price anywhere in the builder's words.
BuySellStartups: it is a marketplace with its own Pricing page and required account, run by Tiny Startup Studio; no grudge posted.
Dotflowy: requires an invite code and account to try; no grudge or Workflowy price mentioned by the builder.
Voicebox: README and HN post contain no grudge and no mention of Wispr Flow's price; also needs a Cloudflare Workers AI account to run and has no license file.
Voquill: 'Backed by Y Combinator' in voquill.com footer, team of 'we', 'Book a call' site — automatic reject.
Startup-seeker: site is behind a Vercel security checkpoint and the builder never states a grudge (a commenter mentioned Crunchbase paid plans, not the builder).
Kanba: HN post has no link and no text; no grudge, nothing to verify
Campsend: has a Pro plan alongside a free tier (15 deliveries/mo) = open-core
It's a Plan: no grudge sentence beyond 'no per-seat fees'; self-hosted team platform, not a consumer app
Bloom (Loom alt): grudge is about hosted-platform lock-in, not price; no price complaint anywhere
CommentCast (Jam.dev alt): no grudge; 'get started for free' implies tiers; hosted dashboard needs account
Ollie: sold as a one-time purchase, not free
StageWhisper Lite: free Lite plus paid Founders edition from the same maker = open-core
BetterQR: great grudge but 3 free codes then a paid tier = open-core
Slidepicker: 'we' team, grudge is PowerPoint UX not price, no named paid victim
Budgie Diet: no named paid victim; grudge is ads and account walls, not a price
Flowrite: quotable subscription grudge but never names the paid app it replaces
BloomDisk: no quotable grudge; only 'paid disk tools often $10-20', DaisyDisk mentioned only as a non-affiliation disclaimer
RookieClip: no grudge sentence on HN or site; site is a JS SPA with a /pricing route I could not render, so free-no-strings is unverifiable
BankToLedger: site returns 404; no grudge on HN
Modor (Placeit alternative): no grudge sentence anywhere in the HN post, just 'I built a free alternative to Placeit'; fails gate 1
TabTab (Toby alternative): empty HN post, zero comments, no grudge in the builder's words; fails gate 1
Whispering (Superwhisper alternative): builder's only stated reason is 'I couldn't find an open-source alternative ... that I liked', which is a preference, not a price grudge; fails gate 1
OpenVitals (Function Health alternative): empty HN post, no builder words at all; fails gate 1
VoiceInk (Superwhisper/Wispr Flow alternative): paid app (commenter: 'How is it open source if you're charging for it?'); fails gate 3
Dyad (Lovable alternative): no grudge ('without the lock-in' is not a price complaint) and Dyad ships its own paid Pro tier; open-core reject
PostPlanify (Buffer alternative): real grudge ('tired of paying $60/mo for Buffer') but the app itself is $39/workspace/month with a 7-day trial; fails gate 3
Retirology (retirement planner): good subscription grudge, but pay-what-you-want with a $19 base price and yearly re-purchase; fails gate 3
Music Buddha (offline music practice apps): free with a tip jar, but no named paid victim and no grudge sentence from the builder; fails gates 1 and 2
S2Q (Stripe-to-QuickBooks): credit bundles from $10/100 credits, made by AI For Verticals, Inc.; fails gate 3 and is a company
Expi (media converter): builder's frustration is about UX and missing features, not price; no named victim; fails gates 1 and 2
FileShot (file sharing): grudge is about email walls, not price, and the site sells Pro/Creator/Professional tiers at $10-$38/mo; open-core reject
Fillvisa: open-core — builder is shipping a paid plus.fillvisa.com tier for immigration professionals (automatic reject).

Minimum Viable Expat: Nomads.com price unverifiable — primary page renders placeholder amounts ($19.99 lite / $1 lifetime via JS), 2026 secondary sources disagree ($99 one-time vs $299.98 lifetime vs 100-200/yr).
Yapper: no grudge sentence anywhere — HN post and README just say 'Built a free alternative to Superwhisper'.
MagicCV.ai: open-core — 'we offer one-time payment options' for more resumes/AI usage, and considering AdSense.
smmall.cloud: has paid plans (larger files, screen sharing, branding) and is built by 'Smmall, an incubator'; no grudge text.
3-Line Calendar: solid grudge ('most of them either ask you to pay... or trick you into some in-app purchase') but no named paid victim on HN, site, or README.
illll (live longer): free and open source but no grudge and no named paid victim.
Skaoot: no grudge; only 'similar to TripIt or Flighty', and it is an account-based travel service.
Vibe Coded My Taxes: self-hosted S-Corp dashboard with no named paid victim.
Gravit Designer clone (studio.wladradchenko.ru): victim (Gravit/Corel Vector) was shut down, so no current price to verify.
Open Right Zoom: no grudge sentence anywhere, just 'I built a free open source alternative'
OpenTrainer: no named victim ('bloated workout apps'), and it has its own Pro tier ('keep Pro free forever') behind a Clerk sign-up
MySigMail: no grudge and no named victim ('expensive email signature tools')
Pure Meditate: grudge and victim fine (Calm), but the App Store listing returns 404 and the iTunes lookup is empty, so the app is unavailable and free/no-IAP cannot be verified
Better Remote Jobs: no specific paid victim named; site sells job posts and ad slots, so it is a business not a free replacement
Splitpro: no grudge sentence on HN or in the README (Splitwise named, no price complaint)
Spliit: no grudge, built 'to learn Go'; no complaint about Splitwise pricing
Phrasing Bot: no grudge sentence in the empty HN post or README
Hi.Events: no grudge in the post; project also runs a hosted paid cloud (open-core)
CoderScreen: own pricing page has Starter $50/mo and Scale $350/mo tiers (open-core), and post asks for teams
YA Copilot: no grudge, 'I wanted a customizable AI assistant' is not a price complaint

Deep Focus (43872133): grudge is real ('tired of productivity tools constantly asking me to sign up, pay monthly') but no specific paid victim is named anywhere in the post or store listing; fails gate 2

Rank and Run (49296795): title says 'no free version of this card game existed' but the post has no text, no comments, and the site never names the paid app it replaces (it is a Liverpool Rummy / Milestone rummy clone); fails gate 2

lean-intros (48126255): built by the founder of Draftboard, a competing commercial warm-intro product ('I'm the founder of ... Draftboard'); company competitor, not a solo grudge; also BYOK Apollo enrichment
Subly (43651119): grudge is forgotten subscription charges, not a paid tool; no victim named; fails gates 1 and 2
Auto Hongmyungbo (47177445): 'Paid tools are expensive, and free ones are too limited' names no victim; org-owned repo (NomaDamas); fails gate 2
Imagev2.me (48046854): credit-based paid image studio with sign-in; fails gate 3
Orcha (46923497): no post text and orcha.nl is down (Vercel 'Payment required / DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED'); cannot verify anything
Just Minesweeper (45253173): grudge is ad-supported app-store clones, not a paid tool; no priced victim; fails gate 2
